newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland agrees to sell Ruch news-stand chain.
newsitem.headline: Poland agrees to sell Ruch news-stand chain.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry said on Friday that it had accepted an offer from a consortium bidding to buy the country's biggest news-stand chain Ruch SA.
The consortium involved is likely to be a group led by Hachette Distribution services, which had a right to be a sole bidder for Ruch until last week and submitted its final purchase offer on Monday.
"The treasury ministry informs that it has accepted a corrected price offer from a consortium interested in purchase of Ruch SA's shares," the statement said, without naming the consortium.
It said the ministry now expected the consortium to provide more details on investment plans and to negotiate a package of social benefits with trade unions.
A ministry press office official said more details on the accepted offer would be available after a sale agreement was signed, but did not say when this could take place.

The Hachette consortium, which also groups several Polish firms, wanted to buy a strategic stake in Ruch, which has a 65 percent share on Poland's press distribution market and owns 17,000 news-stands nationwide.
Ruch's net profit in 1995 was 16.2 million zlotys on sale of 2.7 billion zlotys.
